title: A Preregistered Audit of Dataset Contamination Controls in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired, confirmatory audit to test whether conservative deterministic contamination detectors (exact normalized token equality; fuzzy 5-gram overlap; provenance heuristics) flag items in a reproducible 150-item NetOps sample and whether applying preregistered contamination controls changes validator-based success rates. The preregistered design (study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) specified 150 item pairs (baseline vs guarded), a single hosted model (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"), and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). The run completed 300 episodes (150 pairs) but, because execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) and the sampled items were provenance-stable synthetic tasks, model_calls_used = 150 and no high-confidence contamination flags were produced. All baseline and guarded episodes passed the verifier (baseline = 150/150, guarded = 150/150); paired success-rate difference = 0.0 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 0.0]); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. We reconcile the preregistration→execution artifacts, explain why the run was insensitive to generation-level contamination under the executed semantics, and provide artifact-grounded recommendations (provenance-rich sampling, independent generation per condition, multi-model scope, paraphrase-robust detectors, and increased logging) for audits intended to detect contamination in web-sourced benchmarks.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks (intent-to-configuration translation, automated repair). Reliable operational adoption depends on evidence that benchmarked performance reflects genuine capability rather than dataset contamination (items or templated prompts that appear in model training data) or low-complexity, templated tasks that overstate real-world performance. Recent surveys and benchmark studies call for contamination-aware evaluation designs and verifier-backed oracles.

Research question and contribution. We preregistered and executed an artifact-anchored audit to answer: under conservative deterministic detectors (exact normalized equality; fuzzy 5-gram overlap with preregistered thresholds; provenance timestamp heuristics) and a guarded exclusion policy, (1) how many high-confidence flags arise in a reproducible 150-item NetOps sample, and (2) how much does applying those controls change an LLM's validator pass rate? Our contributions are: (i) a fully preregistered confirmatory experiment (study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) executed end-to-end with archived artifacts; (ii) exact, artifact-verified confirmatory statistics on Npairs = 150 with deterministic validator traces; and (iii) a preregistration→execution reconciliation that explains why this execution produced a degenerate null and prescribes artifact-grounded audit-design changes to increase sensitivity.

Scope and key execution facts. The execution used a deterministic task generator producing synthetic items (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") and set independent_condition_generation = false (shared_initial_candidate semantics). These execution facts are recorded in the archived execution bundle (execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/model_configuration.json). Because no high-confidence flags occurred under the preregistered detectors, the shared generation semantics produced a single model call per item, reducing model_calls_used to 150 (model_calls_used and episode counts are recorded in the execution manifest). These facts materially constrain inference: the observed null does not imply absence of contamination in independent web-sourced benchmarks.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven NetOps and verification. Prior work demonstrates that LLMs can generate configuration artifacts for constrained NetOps problems and that integrating formal or deterministic verifiers (e.g., header-space analysis, subspecification) or iterative validate–repair loops improves average repair quality versus naive generation. System and benchmark papers (example research leads in the field) show both promise and substantial variability stemming from dataset construction, prompting, and verifier choices.

Evaluation validity and contamination. Meta-studies and methodological surveys emphasize two recurring risks: contamination (leakage from benchmark items into model pretraining) and construct invalidity (templated, low-complexity tasks that do not reflect operational difficulty). These works recommend contamination detection (exact matches, n-gram overlaps, provenance checks), paraphrase-sensitive defenses, and richer provenance logging. Our audit implements a conservative subset of these defenses in a preregistered format and uses a deterministic NetOps validator as an oracle for functional correctness.

Positioning. Unlike broad benchmark papers that measure absolute model capability across curated corpora, our experiment is a preregistered methodological audit: we test whether a specific, preregistered set of contamination controls would have altered verifier-measured success on a reproducible sample under the archived execution semantics. We do not claim a prevalence estimate for contamination in public benchmarks because the executed sample and generation semantics were intentionally synthetic and shared (see Methods and Limitations).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration, primary estimand, and sample. The study was preregistered (study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) and frozen prior to execution. The primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) across item×model pairs; the confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test, and we compute a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) per the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. The confirmatory sample size was 150 pairs (planned_episode_count = 300 episodes). The preregistration specified deterministic sampling with fixed seeds and replacement rules for excluded items; the execution used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce provenance-stable synthetic tasks.

Detectors and guarded policy (preregistered). Detectors were: (1) exact normalized token equality after canonicalization; (2) fuzzy 5-gram shingle overlap (Jaccard/overlap) with preregistered high-confidence threshold ≥ 0.80 (and sensitivity points at 0.65 and 0.50); and (3) provenance timestamp heuristics comparing item timestamps to the model cutoff. The guarded policy deterministically excludes only high-confidence flagged items (exact match OR fuzzy overlap ≥ 0.80) and replaces them via deterministic retemplating/topology augmentation from the same generator distribution using fixed seeds. Replacement candidates required embedding-similarity checks per the preregistered plan before acceptance. Detection and replacement behaviors are implemented in transformation_manifest.json and unit-tested in the archived code base.

Generation semantics and verifier. The preregistration permitted deterministic task generators and allowed shared_initial_candidate semantics; the executed run set independent_condition_generation = false. Under this semantics a single shared generation per item is used for both baseline and guarded episodes unless a high-confidence exclusion triggers replacement, in which case the guarded episode would have a deterministically different response. The verifier is deterministic_netops_validator_v5; its scoring rule for intent→configuration tasks is full_intent_constraint_validation (parse→state-update→property checks), returning a binary pass/fail plus detailed traces (observed_touched_field_count, required_command_count, violation codes). Verifier traces for each episode are archived under execution/scoring.

Planned analyses and sensitivities. The prespecified primary confirmatory test is the paired McNemar test with the paired bootstrap CI. Sensitivity analyses included treating failed model calls as failures, evaluating fuzzy-overlap thresholds at 0.50/0.65/0.80, and stratified subgroup analysis by templated vs realistic items (templating detector). The preregistration included a power and precision discussion: multi-model designs were planned to detect ≈5 percentage-point paired differences with 80% power; single-model single-call designs reduce sensitivity and increase the minimum detectable effect. All analysis parameters and their archived locations are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The execution completed planned_episode_count = 300 episodes (150 pairs) with completed_episode_count = 300 and failed_episode_count = 0. Because independent_condition_generation = false and no high-confidence exclusions were triggered, model_calls_used = 150 (one shared generation per item). Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm complete_pair_count = 150 and consistent provider-call accounting (execution/deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Contamination detector outcomes. Under the preregistered detectors, no high-confidence contamination flags were produced for the executed sample. The artifact analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged episodes (empty flagged-rows content). Per the archived detector logging policy, per-item fuzzy-overlap scores were recorded only for episodes that met the flagging criteria or required replacement handling; since no episodes reached the high-confidence threshold, the detector produced no recorded overlap aggregates for the sample. Consequently, we report the artifact-documented absence of high-confidence flags rather than derived per-item overlap statistics.

Verifier outcomes and confirmatory statistics. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 returned pass for all baseline episodes (baseline_success_count = 150/150; baseline_success_rate = 1.0) and for all guarded episodes (guarded_success_count = 150/150; guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 150, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). The primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) = 0.0 percentage points. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. All per-episode responses and validator traces are archived (execution/responses and execution/scoring) and included in the execution bundle.

Representative exemplar. A representative archived episode (pair-000001 / task-000001) shows identical normalized_reference_answer and normalized_response: "interface edge1 admin down\ninterface edge1 vlan 30\ninterface edge1 mtu 1600\ninterface edge1 admin up". The validator returned score = 1 with parsed_command_count = 4 and provided a detailed validator_trace. The exemplar's raw response, scoring JSON, and validator trace are present under execution/responses and execution/scoring and are referenced in the execution manifest.

What the data show (artifact-grounded interpretation). For this execution regime (synthetic items + shared_initial_candidate semantics), the preregistered conservative detectors produced zero high-confidence flags and the validator passed all episodes under both conditions. Those facts are self-consistent and recorded in the archived manifests; however they do not test detector sensitivity to contamination in web-sourced corpora or to paraphrase-level leakage because the sample provenance and generation semantics prevented independent generation comparisons and the detector logging policy suppressed per-item overlap outputs absent flags.
sections.discussion:
Why the result is degenerate (artifact-grounded explanation). Two execution choices explain the degenerate null outcome. First, the confirmatory sample consisted of provenance-stable synthetic tasks generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (source_identifier "synthetic-netops:"), so canonicalized exact matches to public corpus fingerprints and high fuzzy 5-gram overlaps above the preregistered threshold were unlikely. Second, independent_condition_generation = false (shared_initial_candidate), so when no exclusions occurred a single shared generation per item served both baseline and guarded episodes; the archived provider-call accounting and model_call counts confirm this (execution/model_configuration.json and execution/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Together these facts mechanistically produce identical baseline and guarded outputs per item and make the paired test uninformative for generation-level contamination in this run.

Audit lessons and artifact-grounded recommendations. The preregistration→execution artifacts imply concrete, verifiable improvements for audits aimed at detecting contamination in web-sourced benchmarks: (1) sample provenance-rich public items (avoid synthetic provenance) to exercise detectors against real pretraining-era sources; (2) set independent_condition_generation = true so baseline and guarded conditions are independently generated and cannot collapse to a shared output; (3) expand to multiple models and independent seeds to increase discordance signals across model families; (4) record per-item fuzzy-overlap scores regardless of flag status to enable reporting of overlap distributions; and (5) augment deterministic detectors with paraphrase-robust measures and human adjudication for borderline cases. Each recommendation follows from artifacts: the execution manifest, deterministic_reconciliation, and contamination_summary.csv document the limits that motivate these changes.

Operational implications and verifier role. For NetOps practitioners the audit highlights two practical points: (a) verifier-backed validators (such as deterministic_netops_validator_v5) are valuable oracles for functional correctness checks, but passing such validators does not prove production readiness because validators check a prespecified set of properties and may not capture all semantic regressions; and (b) audit sensitivity depends critically on sampling provenance and generation semantics. Designs intended to assess public-benchmark leakage should avoid synthetic provenance and shared-generation semantics and should log detector outputs at a fine granularity.

Threats to validity and what remains untested. Internal validity: prompt sensitivity and generation randomness were constrained by the deliberate use of deterministic generators and shared generation semantics; this reduced variance but also reduced the experiment's ability to reveal generation-level contamination. Construct validity: the detectors implemented conservative heuristics (exact-match and fuzzy 5-gram overlap) and therefore may miss paraphrase-level memorization; the detector logging policy (record overlap scores only when flags occur) limited post-hoc construct assessment. External validity: single-model execution (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic sampling limit generalization to other LLM families and to web-sourced benchmarks. Conclusion validity: the paired test produced no discordant pairs, so statistical evidence regarding H2 is null under these execution choices; planned sensitivity analyses and multi-model designs remain necessary to detect realistic contamination effects.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-anchored paired audit of conservative contamination detectors for LLM-for-NetOps evaluation. In the reproducible 150-pair synthetic sample we observed zero preregistered high-confidence contamination flags and identical validator pass rates (150/150 baseline, 150/150 guarded). The degenerate null outcome is artifact-supported and resulted from provenance-stable synthetic sampling combined with shared_initial_candidate generation semantics; it does not imply absence of contamination in web-sourced benchmarks. We reconcile preregistration→execution artifacts, confirm deterministic reconciliations passed, and provide concrete artifact-grounded recommendations—provenance-rich sampling, independent generation per condition, multi-model scope, paraphrase-sensitive detectors, and detailed detector logging—to increase audit sensitivity in future work. All experiment artifacts, validator traces, analyses, and execution manifests are archived in the execution bundle and available for inspection per the Disclosure Statement below.

limitations: Single-model execution (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across other LLM families, sizes, or training corpora.

Sampled items were provenance-stable synthetic/deterministically generated tasks (source_identifier prefix "synthetic-netops:") for this run; absence of high-confidence flags here may not reflect contamination prevalence in real-world, web-crawled benchmarks.

Generation semantics used shared_initial_candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical model outputs when no exclusions occurred and thus limiting sensitivity to interventions that rely on independent re-generation.

Contamination detection relied on preregistered conservative heuristics (exact match and fuzzy 5-gram overlap thresholds); subtler contamination patterns (paraphrased memorization, partial leakage) may escape these heuristics and require richer provenance or manual adjudication.

Passing the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 indicates satisfaction of the checked functional constraints but does not imply comprehensive production readiness or absence of semantic regressions outside the validator's scope.
